A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show the importance of mechanisms in representation learning, and that we can leverage this to achieve new results for representation learning.
we characterize the sources of nonidentifiability in representation learning, and show how we can leverage knowledge about mechanisms to overcome them.
we study the properties of latent variables from a new angle: the mechanisms that generate them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by leveraging knowledge about mechanisms, we can achieve a much more powerful form of identification than by leveraging knowledge about the latent variables themselves.

by leveraging knowledge of underlying mechanisms, we may be able to design more powerful representation learning algorithms that can learn latent properties even in the presence of complex dependencies.
